Why Do Tigers Spray This Strange Liquid? 🐅 When a tiger sprays urine onto a tree, it isn’t just marking territory—it’s leaving behind a chemical message. The scent can reveal information about the tiger and signal to others that the area is already occupied. This powerful form of scent communication helps tigers defend territory, find potential mates, and avoid unnecessary confrontations in the wild.

videos.caption: Grumpy Kallie is waiting for breakfast. 😊 Today, on International Tiger Day, we’re honored to introduce you to Kallie—a tiger whose survival is nothing short of a miracle. When Kallie was rescued by Lions Tigers & Bears, she had been abandoned and left to die. Her condition was so critical that she required extensive emergency medical care, multiple surgeries, and ultimately a life-saving leg amputation. Against all odds, Kallie never gave up. Today, Kallie is thriving on three legs, living the life she always deserved at Lions Tigers & Bears. She continues to receive specialized daily care from our dedicated team, and every step she takes is a reminder of what’s possible when compassion meets action. Your support made Kallie’s second chance possible. Thank you for standing with us as we rescue, rehabilitate, and provide lifelong sanctuary to animals who have nowhere else to turn. Happy International Tiger Day.

videos.caption: Cats out of the bag … or den! 🐯🐯 Our little tiger ladies are officially on habitat for all guests to see! Zookeepers are following mom, Ndari’s lead on where and how the cubs spend their time. They will have access to the main habitat as well as their behind-the-scenes den, where they may choose to rest or nap.   You may notice modifications to the yard, like extra logs in the water; these “baby proofing” measures are important to help keep little cubs safe in a big space. The cubs have been introduced to shallow pools behind the scenes but are now exploring the larger space for the first time! Since tigers are a solitary species, adults typically only spend time together for breeding, and female tigers are solely involved in cub rearing. Rakan will alternate in the main habitat in the coming weeks, but for now our cubs and mom are taking the front seat.  Stay tuned for more footage of these tiny tigers exploring their huge habitat!
